In the latest trading session, Salesforce (CRM) closed at $241.05, marking a -2.31% move from the previous day. The stock's performance was behind the S&P 500's daily loss of 1.09%. Elsewhere, the Dow saw a downswing of 0.34%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq depreciated by 2.15%.

Coming into today, shares of the customer-management software developer had gained 1.6% in the past month. In that same time, the Computer and Technology sector gained 1.99%, while the S&P 500 gained 2.44%.

The investment community will be closely monitoring the performance of Salesforce in its forthcoming earnings report. It is anticipated that the company will report an EPS of $3.43, marking a 5.54% rise compared to the same quarter of the previous year. Meanwhile, our latest consensus estimate is calling for revenue of $11.46 billion, up 11.72% from the prior-year quarter.

For the entire fiscal year, the Zacks Consensus Estimates are projecting earnings of $16.71 per share and a revenue of $46.25 billion, representing changes of +33.47% and +11.38%, respectively, from the prior year.

Additionally, investors should keep an eye on any recent revisions to analyst forecasts for Salesforce. Recent revisions tend to reflect the latest near-term business trends. With this in mind, we can consider positive estimate revisions a sign of optimism about the business outlook.

Our research demonstrates that these adjustments in estimates directly associate with imminent stock price performance. Investors can capitalize on this by using the Zacks Rank. This model considers these estimate changes and provides a simple, actionable rating system.

Ranging from #1 (Strong Buy) to #5 (Strong Sell), the Zacks Rank system has a proven, outside-audited track record of outperformance, with #1 stocks returning an average of +25% annually since 1988. Within the past 30 days, our consensus EPS projection remained stagnant. Salesforce is currently a Zacks Rank #3 (Hold).

In the context of valuation, Salesforce is at present trading with a Forward P/E ratio of 14.76. This valuation marks a discount compared to its industry average Forward P/E of 21.23.

We can also see that CRM currently has a PEG ratio of 0.86. This metric is used similarly to the famous P/E ratio, but the PEG ratio also takes into account the stock's expected earnings growth rate. Internet - Software stocks are, on average, holding a PEG ratio of 1.25 based on yesterday's closing prices.

The Internet - Software industry is part of the Computer and Technology sector. With its current Zacks Industry Rank of 81, this industry ranks in the top 33% of all industries, numbering over 250.

Salesforce Stock Is Up About 30% Since July 31. Here's Where It Could Go by 2031 ©@Blue Planet Studio from Getty Images via Canva, @Blue Planet Studio from Getty Images via Canva
Key Stats for Salesforce Stock

Current Price: $246.74

Target Price (Mid): ~$445

Street Target: ~$286

Potential Total Return: ~81%

Annualized IRR: ~15% / year

What Happened?

Salesforce (CRM:NYSE) closed at $246.74 on October 15, 2026, up 4.57% on the day and 34.08% above its July 31 close of $184.02. Most of that run came on August 27, when shares jumped 22.58% after second-quarter results. The October 15 close sits 2.11% below that day's $252.05.

No Salesforce-specific catalyst was confirmed for October 15. The gain came with the sector: ServiceNow (NOW) closed up 6.14% as investors rotated into enterprise software amid a sell-off in semiconductor shares.

Evidence from Salesforce's September investor session, available through its investor relations materials, suggests AI usage is running ahead of what Salesforce bills for it.

Salesforce Drawdowns (TIKR)
Salesforce's Top AI Customers Roughly Doubled Their ARR, but Billing Trails Usage

Robin Washington, President and Chief Operating and Financial Officer, spoke about the top 100 customers by Agentic Work Units, Salesforce's measure of the work its agents complete. Among them, she said, "within 18 months of Agentforce's launch, we're seeing ARR uplift about 2x as to what it was." As customers become agentic enterprises, she sees "a 3x to 4x opportunity for that ARR uplift" over several years.

The cohort is selected by usage, and Washington did not limit the annual recurring revenue figure to AI products. It shows what is possible, not what the average customer pays.

The lag comes from contract design. President and Chief Revenue Officer Alexa Vignone said that in Q2, "7 of our 10 largest deals were AELAs." AELAs are flat, seat-based agentic enterprise license agreements. President and Chief Operating Officer Miguel Milano added that "Contract lengths are increasing." In January, a Gartner analyst said she expects these capped deals to convert into defined-quantity contracts at renewal. Salesforce responded that its consumption-based AI pricing is tied to business outcomes.

Adecco and Siemens Show Where Repricing Comes From

Adecco Group (ADEN) runs 7 agents in 12 countries. Pierre Matuchet, its Senior Vice President of IT, said those agents cut the time to present candidates by 40% and lifted its fill rate by 10%. Adecco has decided to roll out Coworker to 27,000 users, which Milano said it could switch on under an edition it already owned.

Separately, Adecco's two-year AELA, signed seven months before the session, carries "unlimited credit for all these use cases." Milano's renewal pitch: "What if we agree on a couple of metrics and then we share in your success?" That is a proposal, not a signed contract.

Salesforce (CRM) is back in focus after partners ZoomInfo, Demandbase and Docusign deepened their integrations with Hunter and Agentforce, pulling more sales and contract workflows into Salesforce's AI driven environment.

Recent moves in Salesforce's share price tell a mixed story. The stock has gained 4.57% on a 1 day share price return and 8.31% over 7 days, yet it is down 3.49% on a 30 day share price return and 2.71% year to date. At the same time, the 44.49% 90 day share price return and 1.15% 1 year total shareholder return point to momentum that has cooled but not disappeared as the market weighs fresh AI deals, acquisitions like Loops, and big customer wins such as the long term HMRC agreement against ongoing questions about growth quality and efficiency.

Scan how Salesforce's AI partnerships compare with other potential breakouts across enterprise software by reviewing the curated list of 55 AI infrastructure stocks that are shaping tomorrow's revenue workflows.

Salesforce now trades around a 16% discount to analyst targets and a deeper estimated intrinsic gap near 52%. Is that a margin of safety, or a warning that the market's caution on quality and efficiency still has teeth?

Most Popular Narrative: 4% Undervalued

Against a last close of $246.74, the most followed fair value on Salesforce sits near $255.90. According to michaelyang, this leaves a small discount that hinges less on aggressive forecasts and more on simple survival.

The per-seat licence was only ever the toll booth. The asset is the governed system of record: every customer, every deal, every entitlement, for about 80% of the Fortune 500. And the one thing an autonomous AI agent cannot do is act on a customer without getting into that record first. An agent with no permissions, no governance and no audit trail is not an asset, it is a liability waiting to happen. So the same automation wave that threatens the seat count is exactly what drives every serious enterprise deeper into the data layer Salesforce owns. The meter changes from per-person to per-action. It does not disappear.

stock trading market equity wall street -Shutterstock

(Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

The Nasdaq Composite plunged Friday, halting its four-week rally, amid a technology sell-off on Wall Street.

The index declined 2.1% to 26,140.03. The S&P 500 fell 1.1% to 7,659.44, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 0.3% to 52,002.41.

Among sectors, tech led the laggards, while energy paced the gainers.

This week, the Nasdaq tumbled 4.5%, ending its four-week winning streak. That weekly performance marked the worst since June.

The S&P 500 ended the week down 1.9% and the Dow gained 0.7%.

Alphabet (GOOGL), Salesforce (CRM), Cisco Systems (CSCO), Microsoft (MSFT), Amazon (AMZN), and Nvidia (NVDA) were the biggest decliners on the Dow.

Micron Technology (MU), Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Sandisk (SNDK) also fell.

The S&P 500 and the Nasdaq Composite hit fresh closing highs Oct. 6, but the rally had been powered by only a few tech giants, suggesting underlying weakness on Wall Street.

Many analysts fear a potential stock market correction as the majority of S&P 500 stocks have been hovering well below all-time highs.

Treasury yields were mixed. The two-year rate fell 3.2 basis points at 4.72%, while the 10-year rate was unchanged at 5.09%.

US industrial production grew more than expected in September as manufacturing output rebounded despite weakness in the auto component, Federal Reserve data showed.

Brent crude jumped 3.4% to $109.53 a barrel in Friday late-afternoon trade, while West Texas Intermediate was 3.8% higher at $101.64. Both benchmarks were up for the week, with Brent on track for its fourth consecutive weekly increase.

Saudi Arabia intercepted multiple missiles and drones on Friday, including a missile heading toward the oil export terminal Yanbu, CNBC reported, citing a military spokesperson.

US lawmakers introduced a bill Friday to block President Donald Trump's deal to allow export of hundreds of millions of barrels of Russian diesel, Bloomberg News reported.

Spot gold fell 0.1% to $4,166.56 per troy ounce, while silver remained steady at $57.14 per ounce.
